title: Rational Exponents and Radicals: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Rational Exponents and Radicals: Visual Guide

1. From Count To Fraction | sliders for the base b and the numerator m and denominator n of the exponent, with the fraction marked on a number line of integer rungs and both evaluation orders worked out | a rational exponent is forced by the nesting rule: the denominator roots and the numerator powers, and the value lands between the whole-number powers you already owned

2. Rules That Survive | five candidate exponent rules, each tested live as you drag a, b, m and n, with the two sides shown agreeing or splitting apart | one numeric disagreement refutes a rule forever while agreement proves nothing, and the true ones, (ab)^r = a^r b^r and a^m · a^n = a^(m+n), never part under a sweep

3. Square Then Check | sqrt(x + p) = d and sqrt(x + p) = x + q with sliders, both branches of the squared equation drawn and every candidate marked as checking or extraneous | squaring also solves the sign-flipped mirror equation, so every candidate must go back into the original, and a candidate survives exactly when the two sides come out with the same sign

4. Match The Base | b^(x + k) = target with base, shift and target controls, the exponential curve crossing the horizontal target line exactly once | rewriting both sides on one base works because b^x is one-to-one; b = 1 degenerates to every x or none, and a target that is not a power of the base is trapped between two integers, the gap logarithms fill
